newsitem.title: CHINA: China ends ban on U.S. poultry imports.
newsitem.headline: China ends ban on U.S. poultry imports.

text.p: China has ended its ban on imports of poultry and related products from two American states, the China Daily said on Tuesday.
The ban was imposed on imports from Missouri and Oklahoma in December in response to what China said was an outbreak of Newcastle disease in poultry in the two states.

"The U.S. cleaned up the last Newcastle case on September 27 last year and ensured that this would not happen again," the newspaper quoted an official of the China Administration of Animal and Plant Quarantine as saying.
China had said that five cases of the virulent disease had been discovered in Missouri and Oklahoma between July and September last year.
U.S. officials had said they had been trying to persuade Chinese authorities to lift the ban on poultry because the outbreak had only affected pet birds.
China had also ordered a ban on all U.S. poultry brought into the country by travellers. This restriction was also removed under the latest ruling.
China is the second biggest export market in the world, after Russia, for U.S. poultry goods.
